body: A real thing called foxfire: fungi in damp rotting wood glowing a cold blue-green, reportedly bright enough in places to read by. People had watched it for centuries before anyone looked properly — in 1823 the glowing beams in a mine turned out to be fungus. The tail has requested foxfire for the workshop, as a treat.

receipts.title: Wikipedia — Foxfire
quote: After many more literary references to foxfire by early scientists and naturalists, its cause was discovered in 1823. The glow emitted from wooden support beams in mines was examined, and it was found that the luminescence came from fungal growth.
Although generally very dim, in some cases foxfire is bright enough to read by.
